title: Boyle's Law (Gas Laws)
notes: This textbook page introduces Boyle's Law, which explains the mathematical relationship between the pressure and volume of a gas when temperature is held constant.
Here is a comprehensive summary of the core concepts, formula derivations, and significance shown on the page:
• Statement: The volume of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure, provided the temperature remains constant.
• Core Concept: If you increase the pressure on a gas, its volume decreases proportionally. If you decrease the pressure, its volume increases.

• The Formula: Density (d) is defined as mass divided by volume (d = m/V), meaning volume is inversely proportional to density (V = m/d).

• The Rule: At a constant temperature, the density of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional to its pressure. If you double the pressure, you pack twice as many gas molecules into the same space, doubling the density.

• Syringes: When you pull the plunger of a syringe back, the volume inside increases, causing the internal pressure to drop. The higher atmospheric pressure outside pushes the liquid into the syringe.

• Breathing Mechanism: When you inhale, your diaphragm expands your lungs, increasing their volume. This lowers the internal air pressure, drawing outside air in. When you exhale, lung volume decreases, pressure increases, and air is pushed out.

• Scuba Diving: As a diver goes deeper underwater, the ambient pressure increases significantly. If a diver ascends too quickly while holding their breath, the decreasing water pressure causes the air trapped in their lungs to rapidly expand in volume, which can cause severe lung damage.

• High Altitude Behavior: At high altitudes, atmospheric pressure is low. Consequently, weather balloons or passenger aircraft cabins must account for the fact that gases expand dramatically under reduced external pressure.
